text:
Maya L.: Quick sync on VertexMed POC kick-off tomorrow 9:30am PT. Need to lock success criteria, test prompts, confirm security Q answers, and clarify trial pricing/credits before call. Agenda draft below.

Diego R.: What's their expected throughput? They mentioned ~80 qps burst for 2-3 minutes in their doc. That will affect our batching config.

Hannah W.: I skimmed their security questionnaire. Main items: encryption in transit + at rest, audit logs retention (they asked for 1 year), SCIM/SSO requirements, and proof of vulnerability scanning. They want a contact for SOC2 scope.

Ethan: For success metrics they want: 95th percentile latency <250ms for 256-token chat, cost target <$0.75 per 1k tokens, and model accuracy >85% on their clinical-intent prompt set. They also want reproducible eval harness.

Maya L.: Good to be specific. Hannah, can you confirm if our retention policy with 90-day logs will be acceptable, or do we need extended retention for POC? If not, we may need to offer export.

Hannah W.: We can offer export of audit logs for the POC. For SOC2 we can provide the public report and point them to our compliance page. I'll draft responses and tag legal for HSM/KMS questions.

Priya S.: Pricing: Sales recommends a $7k credit + 25% POC discount. Also offer a 'burst allowance' for the 80 qps to avoid throttling. Approve?

Diego R.: For the throughput, suggest we recommend a paired Dedicated pool with autoscale rules: min 2 GPUs, burst to 4 for 5 mins. For the demo, we'll pre-warm KV caches. That should keep tails low.

Ethan: Eval plan: 250 core prompts + 30 adversarial. We'll measure pass/fail and false-positive rate for clinical extraction intents. I'll prepare the set and a reproducible Jupyter runner.

Maya L.: Can someone own SSO onboarding? They want SCIM provisioning and Okta SAML. That's often the blocker for enterprise test accounts.

Priya S.: I'll own SSO onboarding. Assigning @Diego to coordinate with the dev team on IP allowlist and VPN creds.

Hannah W.: Security note: They requested vulnerability scan evidence — we can provide recent internal scan summaries and a contact from infra security. Flagging that to @Ethan to collect artifacts.

Diego R.: Runbook snippet I'll use for smoke test:
```
# smoke test example
python -m poc_runner --model rwd-3b --prompts ./prompts/vertex_core.csv --out results.csv
```

Ethan: I'll run baseline tests overnight against rwd-3b and rwd-4b and post results by 6pm PT.

Maya L.: Confirm stakeholders: VertexMed - Priya (CTO), Jonah (Security Lead), Liza (Data Lead). Our side: Maya, Diego, Hannah, Ethan, Priya S. Invite sent.

Priya S.: Action items: Diego -> infra scaling + IP list; Hannah -> SQ answers + log export plan; Ethan -> eval harness + baseline results by 18:00; Maya -> finalize commercial credits in SFDC. Escalate blockers to me. :thumbsup:
